spec.setup: Start perf-lab with -Xmx128m and drive /api/churn, the allocation-heavy endpoint, at 50 users. The small heap plus sustained allocation keeps the collector busy: gc_pause_count climbs steadily and heap_used_peak_bytes sits near the ceiling, while the HikariCP fields stay entirely ordinary.
spec.notes: Watch the collector's max_recent_ms caveat on this fixture specifically. Micrometer's MAX is a rolling ~2-minute maximum that decays, so a GC pause early in a 300 s window has aged out by the time the window ends -- the collector names the field max_recent_ms rather than max_ms for exactly this reason, and GC is the cause where the under-reporting bites hardest. The count and the mean over the window are the fields that carry the signal here; the max is the one that will look smaller than the run felt.

window.max_recent_ms_note: rolling ~2-minute maximum read at end of window, NOT the maximum over the measured window. Micrometer's MAX decays, so a spike early in the window has already aged out. Under-reports transient causes such as GC pauses; approximates the true window max only for sustained ones.

hikaricp.note: not sampled during load: pending, active, idle. null means the sampler never ran, not that the value was zero.

available_evidence.trace_reason: no trace provider configured for this campaign
notes: gauge peaks for 'datadog' are post-run point reads, not mid-run samples; peaks may understate pressure during the window
